html:
The Kaohsiung incident was a rally for democracy in Kaohsiung, southern Taiwan, on Human Rights Day, 10 December 1979, which ended in clashes with police and the arrest of the opposition's leaders.

The rally was organised by the people behind Formosa Magazine, the voice of the dangwai, the opposition outside the ruling Kuomintang under martial law. Its leaders, among them Shih Ming-teh and Annette Lu, were tried in military courts and given long sentences.

The trials backfired. Their defence lawyers, among them Chen Shui-bian and Frank Hsieh, became politicians, and with the defendants they founded the Democratic Progressive Party in 1986. Annette Lu became vice president and Chen president in 2000, the first time the Kuomintang lost power, a path opened by the election of 1996.
sum: The Kaohsiung incident was a rally for democracy in Kaohsiung, southern Taiwan, on Human Rights Day, 10 December 1979, which ended in clashes with police and the arrest of the opposition's leaders.
